package_info.why_malicious: The package is a malicious Google Apps Script integration injected into an e-commerce website, designed to intercept and exfiltrate customer payment card data to an attacker-controlled domain. This constitutes a web skimming (Magecart-style) attack, violating PCI compliance and exposing sensitive financial information.

execution_context.trigger: HTTP POST request to checkout endpoint (runtime)
execution_context.file_location: Google Apps Script project bound to e-commerce checkout form (e.g., Code.gs in cloud function)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a POST request to the checkout endpoint, the code extracts payment card data from the request parameters and sends it via an outbound HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script intercepts payment card data submitted by customers and transmits it to an unauthorized external domain, a hallmark of web skimming attacks. The use of UrlFetchApp to send sensitive data outside the organization is highly anomalous for payment processing scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce scripts should securely process payment data and only communicate with trusted, PCI-compliant payment processors. They must never transmit cardholder data to unknown or untrusted third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate use would involve sending payment data directly to a certified payment gateway (e.g., Stripe, PayPal) using secure APIs, not to arbitrary external URLs.
key_indicators: Google Apps Script doPost handler accessing payment card fields
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to non-payment-processor domains
Use of UrlFetchApp to transmit sensitive data externally
Script embedded in e-commerce checkout workflow but not part of official payment integration

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects a malicious Google Apps Script into the backend of the e-commerce website, binding it to the checkout form.
attack_chain.leads_to: The script is positioned to intercept customer payment card data during checkout.

attack_chain.action: When a customer submits payment information, the malicious script captures the card data from the HTTP POST request parameters.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive payment card data is extracted by the attacker-controlled script.

attack_chain.action: The script sends the stolen payment card data via an outbound HTTPS POST request to an attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives the exfiltrated payment card data and can monetize it through fraud or resale.

behavioral_signatures: Google Apps Script projects with doPost or doGet handlers making outbound network requests containing payment or card fields
Unexpected POST requests to external domains from scripts associated with e-commerce checkout processes
Use of UrlFetchApp to transmit sensitive data outside the organization's domain
file_indicators: Google Apps Script files (e.g., Code.gs) with handlers accessing payment fields such as cardNumber, cvv, or expiry
Scripts embedded in e-commerce platforms that are not part of official or documented payment integrations
Presence of external domain URLs in script source code not associated with legitimate payment processors
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests from Google Apps Script endpoints to domains not associated with known payment processors
Unusual traffic patterns from e-commerce checkout scripts to unknown or newly registered external servers
DNS lookups or connections to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., attacker.com/collect)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor e-commerce platforms for unauthorized or undocumented Google Apps Script integrations, especially those with doPost or doGet handlers. Inspect script source code for outbound network requests (UrlFetchApp) containing payment-related fields. Alert on POST requests to external domains not on an allowlist of legitimate payment processors. Use network monitoring to detect exfiltration attempts from cloud-based scripts, and flag any scripts referencing external domains not associated with the business or its payment partners.
